title: Streaming session checkpointing & adaptive windowing to prevent partial-output regressions
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: A weekend capacity event (2026-02-22) caused a class of streaming responses to terminate mid-output for ~3% of active sessions. Symptoms were truncated/partial outputs and missing final token sequences that clients interpreted as disconnects. This ticket tracks the post-incident follow-ups: short-term mitigations already rolled, medium-term resiliency features, and longer-term guardrails to prevent recurrence.

Root cause (short): A combination of aggressive backpressure throttling on overloaded GPU workers and a recent batching optimization that moved prefix-commit semantics later in the pipeline. When a worker reclaimed KV cache memory under load, session progress markers were not flushed atomically, leaving a window where the client received partial tokens and the server dropped half-committed outputs.

Impact: Host API customers using streaming for long-form generation experienced truncated responses and client-side retry storms. Internal telemetry showed a 14% spike in session reconnect attempts and an outage-equivalent user impact for heavy prompt workloads.

What we changed immediately (rolled during incident):
- Scoped backpressure thresholds to the pre-optimization profile (hotfix #GH-1529) to reduce immediate partial-commit windows.
- Turned off the non-atomic batch-commit path for affected model families.
- Deployed a temporary per-session tombstone that forces a deterministic reconnect behavior (deployed runtime-1.22-hotfix).

Why the hotfix is not sufficient: The hotfix reduces frequency but does not remove the underlying race between memory reclamation and commit visibility. We need deterministic session checkpointing and client-visible commit markers.

Planned medium-term solution (this ticket): Implement sliding-window session checkpointing and adaptive output windowing. Core ideas: 1) prefix-commit markers: emit a small, durable commit message for every N tokens so clients can detect and request continuation from the last committed marker; 2) sliding checkpoint: maintain an in-memory sliding checkpoint per session that is atomically snapshot-on-evict; 3) adaptive windowing: dynamically tune the commit frequency and in-flight window based on worker memory pressure and observed token-loss rates.

Trade-offs considered:
- More frequent commits reduce risk of partial outputs but increase I/O and slightly higher latency per commit. We plan to make frequency adaptive to limit the cost impact.
- Strong consistency at the server-side (full durable commit each token) would be safest but imposes unacceptable latency and cost. The sliding-checkpoint approach is a middle ground.

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Design doc in Confluence: "Sliding checkpoints & adaptive windowing" (attachment).
- Implementation: runtime changes to emit prefix-commit markers and per-session sliding checkpoints.
- Client SDK changes: lightweight resume API to continue from last commit marker and clearer streaming terminal events.
- E2E tests: chaos injection tests (worker eviction, network partitions) validating no partial-output without a commit marker; performance regression suite.
- Dashboard: Grafana panel for token-commit-latency, commit-frequency-per-session, and partial-output-rate per model.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Notes on compatibility: Prefix-commit markers are additive to existing streaming framing; clients that don't implement resume will see the same final stream semantics but will benefit from improved stability. We will coordinate SDK releases (js + python) to land within one week of runtime rollout.

Longer-term: Consider moving checkpoint persistence to a small redis-backed sidecar for cross-worker resume of long sessions (>5k tokens) and adding a SLO that bounds token-loss probability for streaming endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Runtime and SDK leads
Runtime PR implements sliding checkpoint and emits prefix-commit markers with config flags
Client SDKs accept a resume_from_commit API and gracefully handle commit markers
E2E chaos tests demonstrate <0.01% partial-output rate under simulated worker evictions for baseline traffic
Grafana dashboard shows token-commit-latency and commit-frequency metrics; alert on commit-latency > 200ms
